articles.title: Oregon State vs Utah State: Reichle's Third Touchdown Run Makes the Beavers Bowl Eligible, 31-24
articles.byline: Juniper Ostrowski, The Oregon State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Oregon State Beavers (6-5) 31, Utah State Aggies (4-7) 24, Sat., Nov. 21, Reser Stadium, Corvallis. Next: at Fresno State, Sat., Nov. 28, 10:00 PM ET, Valley Children's Stadium, Fresno
articles.text:
Reser was loud at the end, and I hope the folks on the hill heard it all the way down into town. The Oregon State Beavers beat the Utah State Aggies 31-24 on Saturday night in Corvallis, scored the last 14 points, and we are bowl eligible at 6-5, 4-3 in the Pac-12. I've waited all fall to write that sentence.

We made it harder than it had to be. Utah State went three-and-out first, then Maalik Murphy was intercepted on our third snap by Bobby Arnold, who took it 28 yards to our 25, and Anthony Garcia threw a 25-yard touchdown to Javen Jacobs. McCae Hillstead added a 7-yard run early in the second, and it was 14-0 Aggies. That's a hole you can feel in your stomach.

We climbed out of it the long way. Caleb Ojeda made a 45-yard field goal, and Murphy found Cynai Thomas for a 29-yard touchdown to make it 14-10. Utah State got a 21-yard field goal from Kian Afrookhteh as the half ended, 17-10. Then we took the second-half kickoff 73 yards, and Jake Reichle scored from 4 yards to tie it 17-17.

Hillstead hit Garcia for a 10-yard touchdown at 12:37 of the fourth, and they led 24-17. Murphy answered with a 42-yard throw to Adonis McDaniel, and four plays later Reichle scored from a yard out at 10:03 to tie it again. Utah State stalled on fourth down at our 30 with 6:26 left. We kept coming, and Reichle walked in from 2 yards at 3:41. That was the 31-24 lead, and that was the ballgame.

Reichle ran 13 times for 28 yards and three touchdowns. The yards were short. The scores were huge. Murphy went 20 of 29 for 276 yards, one touchdown throw and one interception. Logan Knapp blocked a 22-yard field goal try in the first quarter, and Drake Vickers picked off Hillstead in the third. After we got the lead, they never got the ball back. We even fell on our own fumble and took a couple of knees.

Next up: at Fresno State, Saturday, Nov. 28, at 10:00 PM ET at Valley Children's Stadium in Fresno. Bowl teams keep working. Go Beavs!

articles.title: Arizona State vs Oklahoma State: Harris and Fette Build a 24-7 Lead, Sun Devils Fall in Overtime 30-27
articles.byline: Skylar Vanterpool, The Arizona State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Oklahoma State Cowboys (7-4) 30, Arizona State Sun Devils (6-5) 27, Sat., Nov. 21, Mountain America Stadium, Tempe. Next: at Arizona, Sat., Nov. 28, 9:00 PM ET, Casino Del Sol Stadium, Tucson
articles.text:
That one hurts because we had it. The Arizona State Sun Devils led the Oklahoma State Cowboys 24-7 at halftime on Saturday night at Mountain America Stadium, and we lost 30-27 in overtime. Our record sits at 6-5 and 4-4 in league play, and a night that felt like a launch turned into a long walk to the parking lot.

The first half was everything I wanted. After William Mason's 13-yard run put the Cowboys up 7-0, Jake Fette found Reed Harris for a 1-yard touchdown, kept it himself from a yard out, and hit Harris on a 60-yard scoring throw. Smith drilled a 51-yard field goal as time expired in the second quarter, and it was 24-7. Harris caught 11 balls for 172 yards and two scores. Fette went 17 of 28 for 232 yards and those two touchdown throws. We converted all five of our fourth downs. Martell Hughes picked off Drew Mestemaker. This was our building.

We just couldn't put it away. Caleb Hawkins scored from 9 yards, Sam Keltner made a 25-yarder, and Hawkins punched in a 7-yard run with 9:11 left, and just like that it was 24-24. Smith put us back in front 27-24 from 38 yards at 3:12, which is the kick I wanted in that moment. Keltner tied it again from 43 at 1:11.

In overtime, Keltner made a 35-yard field goal, 30-27. We got the ball, and Hammonds came down with an interception at the Oklahoma State 21. Cardae Mack had run for 66 yards on 16 carries and given us tough yards all night. The last snap went the other way. That's a cruel way to end it.

Coach Kenny Dillingham said of Fette, "He thinks that game's on him and it's not on him at all. The kid played really, really good football. There's so many things that could have changed the outcome of that game, not just the final play." I'll second that. This loss is on more than one throw.

Owen Long and Hughes each made 12 tackles. We did enough good work to win. We didn't do it for 60 minutes, and then we didn't do it in overtime either.

Next up: at Arizona, Saturday, Nov. 28, at 9:00 PM ET at Casino Del Sol Stadium in Tucson. The Territorial Cup is sitting there. Forks up. Let's go get that one.

articles.title: Oklahoma State vs Arizona State: Keltner Hits in Overtime, Hammonds Ends It, Cowboys Rally 30-27
articles.byline: Dusty Lockridge, The Oklahoma State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Oklahoma State Cowboys (7-4) 30, Arizona State Sun Devils (6-5) 27, Sat., Nov. 21, Mountain America Stadium, Tempe. Next: vs Kansas, Sat., Nov. 28, 6:15 PM ET, Boone Pickens Stadium, Stillwater
articles.text:
I had my head in my hands at halftime, and I'm not ashamed of it. The Oklahoma State Cowboys trailed the Arizona State Sun Devils 24-7 in Tempe on Saturday night, and then we chipped, and chipped, and found a 30-27 win in overtime at Mountain America Stadium. We're 7-4, 5-3 in the Big 12, and this is the kind of night you tell people about in Stillwater for years.

It started fine. William Mason ran 13 yards for a touchdown on the opening drive, and I thought, here we go. Then Jake Fette and Reed Harris took the building. Fette hit Harris for a 1-yard score, ran one in from a yard, and found Harris again from 60 yards. Smith knocked through a 51-yard field goal as the half expired, and it was 24-7. Drew Mestemaker, playing after a right shoulder injury last week, threw an interception to Martell Hughes. We looked stuck.

The second half was a different team. Caleb Hawkins scored from 9 yards in the third, Sam Keltner made a 25-yard field goal, and Hawkins ran in from 7 yards at 9:11 of the fourth to tie it 24-24. Hawkins carried 22 times for 98 yards and those two scores. Mestemaker finished 30 of 40 for 294 yards. Justin Bowick caught seven balls for 95.

Smith put Arizona State back in front 27-24 with a 38-yard field goal at 3:12. Keltner answered from 43 yards at 1:11, and we went to overtime tied at 27. Keltner, who was 3 for 3, opened overtime with a 35-yarder to make it 30-27. On the next snap, Quinton Hammonds came down with an interception at our 21. That was the ballgame. Hammonds also made eight tackles. Jerry Lawson had two sacks.

Coach Eric Morris said, "We were so flat in the first half. We battled back one play at a time in the second half and found a way to win it." That's exactly how it felt from my seat.

Next up: Kansas at Boone Pickens Stadium, Saturday, Nov. 28, at 6:15 PM ET. Get to Stillwater early and make it loud. Go Pokes!

articles.title: Boise State vs San Diego State: Broncos Lead Late, Fall on a Final Kick, 22-20
articles.byline: Thatcher Bluestem, The Boise State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: San Diego State Aztecs (6-5) 22, Boise State Broncos (9-2) 20, Sat., Nov. 21, Albertsons Stadium, Boise. Next: at Colorado State, Sat., Nov. 28, 6:00 PM ET, Canvas Stadium, Fort Collins
articles.text:
That one is going to sting in the hills above Albertsons Stadium for a while. The Boise State Broncos let a home game slip away, 22-20, to the San Diego State Aztecs on our own blue turf, on a 42-yard field goal by Cooper DiLeva as time expired. We're 9-2 and 6-1 in the Pac-12, and a game we had in hand got away in the last two minutes.

We did so many things right. Maddux Madsen scored from a yard out to make it 7-0. After Stone Saunders tied it with a 9-yard run, Canaan Moore answered from 52 yards, and later he added a 26-yarder. Madsen hit Akeem Wright for a 30-yard touchdown early in the fourth, and with 3:53 left we led 20-13. Moore was 2 for 2. Madsen threw for 311 yards. Dylan Riley ran for 69 and caught five balls for 89. Travis Anderson made 11 tackles and picked off Saunders once.

We just didn't finish it. Saunders hit Jaylon Hawkins on a 39-yard scoring throw with 1:51 to go, the two-point try failed, and it was 20-19. We recovered the onside kick. All we needed was a first down. Instead we went for it on fourth down at the Aztecs' 45, and they dropped Madsen for a loss of a yard. They got 24 yards to Jackson Ford, and DiLeva ended it from 42.

I can argue the fourth-down call all night, and I probably will. We had been living with that kind of nerve all year. This time it didn't work. That one is on the whole group, not just one play.

The harder part is how we got there. Madsen threw two interceptions, to Mike Lindsay and Isaiah Green, and he lost a fumble inside the Aztecs' 10 in the first quarter after Brady Nassar knocked it loose and Caleb Ricks fell on it. Three giveaways at home. You don't get to play like that against a team that came to ruin your night, and San Diego State came to ruin it.

We're still 9-2. That matters. It just doesn't feel like it tonight.

Next up: at Colorado State, Saturday, Nov. 28, at 6:00 PM ET at Canvas Stadium in Fort Collins. Shake this off, get on the bus, and be ourselves again. Go Broncos!

articles.title: San Diego State vs Boise State: DiLeva Wins It as Time Expires, Aztecs Stun No. 15 Broncos 22-20
articles.byline: Kai Delgado-Sorensen, The San Diego State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: San Diego State Aztecs (6-5) 22, Boise State Broncos (9-2) 20, Sat., Nov. 21, Albertsons Stadium, Boise. Next: at Washington State, Sat., Nov. 28, 6:30 PM ET, Martin Stadium, Pullman
articles.text:
I am still hoarse, and I do not care. The San Diego State Aztecs beat the No. 15 Boise State Broncos 22-20 on Saturday night at Albertsons Stadium, on their blue turf, with Cooper DiLeva's 42-yard field goal going through as time expired. We're 6-5, 5-2 in the Pac-12, and we just punched a ticket to the conference championship game.

This was a 60-minute fight, just like our coach said afterward. Boise State scored first, Maddux Madsen sneaking in from a yard out early in the second quarter. We didn't flinch. Stone Saunders ran 9 yards to tie it at 7-7 in the third, and then the kickers went to work. Canaan Moore hit from 52, DiLeva answered from 51, and we were 10-10.

Madsen found Akeem Wright for 30 yards early in the fourth, and it was 17-10 Broncos. DiLeva made a 29-yarder, Moore made a 26-yarder, and with the clock melting it was 20-13. I won't lie to you. I started doing the math in my head, and I didn't like it.

Then Saunders went and found Jaylon Hawkins for 39 yards at 1:51. Hawkins had six catches for 89 yards. The two-point try failed, so it was 20-19, and our onside kick bounced to them. Boise State went for it on fourth down from our 45, and Madsen was stopped for a 1-yard loss. Saunders hit Jackson Ford for 24 yards, and DiLeva, who had missed a 49-yarder in the first quarter, drilled the 42-yarder with no time left.

Saunders went 19 of 37 for 227 yards and that touchdown throw, and he ran for 41 yards and a score. Javion Kinnard added 86 yards on 13 carries. Tano Letuli made 10 tackles. Mike Lindsay and Isaiah Green each came down with an interception, and Brady Nassar forced a Madsen fumble that Caleb Ricks recovered. We took the ball away three times.

Our coach said, "We knew it was going to be a 60-minute fight, and we used every single second of what it was, to find a way to win. Even better, we have punched our ticket to come back here in two weeks and partake in the first Pac-12 championship against a really good team." That's the sentence I'm going to sleep on.

First things first. Next up: at Washington State, Saturday, Nov. 28, at 6:30 PM ET at Martin Stadium in Pullman. Then we get Boise State again, on this same turf, in the title game. Go Aztecs!

articles.title: TCU vs Utah: Payne Runs Us Even, then No. 2 Utah Pulls Away, 38-17
articles.byline: Ryder Galloway, The TCU Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Utah Utes (11-0) 38, TCU Horned Frogs (5-6) 17, Sat., Nov. 21, Amon G. Carter Stadium, Fort Worth. Next: at Texas Tech, Thu., Nov. 26, 8:00 PM ET, Galaxy Stadium, Lubbock
articles.text:
I believed, Horned Frog fans, I really did. The TCU Horned Frogs had the Utah Utes tied 17-17 at Amon G. Carter Stadium on Saturday night, and then the Utes scored 21 points before I could catch my breath and left town with a 38-17 win. We're 5-6, 3-5 in the Big 12, and that one is going to sit with me for a while.

The first half was a slog. We didn't score. Utah got a 45-yard field goal from Dillon Curtis, a 4-yard Devon Dampier run, and a 68-yard throw from Dampier to Braden Pegan, and it was 17-0 at the break. It felt heavy in the stands.

Then Jeremy Payne reminded everybody who we are. He took one 43 yards for a touchdown in the third, then scored from 8 yards, and Kyle Lemmermann knocked through a 32-yarder with 9:26 left in the fourth to make it 17-17. Payne finished with 12 carries for 108 yards. Jordan Dwyer caught five balls for 55 yards. For a stretch there, we had this building rocking.

We just couldn't get the stop. Hunter Andrews walked it in from the 2 with 5:46 left. Dampier hit Larry Simmons for 85 yards at 2:59. Jackson Bennee, who intercepted Adam Schobel twice, cleared the way for Dampier's 10-yard score with 1:53 left. Just like that, it was 38-17.

Schobel made his first career start with Jaden Craig out with a knee injury. He went 15 of 31 for 106 yards and those two interceptions. That's a hard assignment against this Utah team, and I won't hang it all on a freshman. Our defense couldn't get off the field when it had to, and we gave the ball away twice. Utah did not give it away at all.

Coach Sonny Dykes said it after the game: "Our job's always to win these games. But our guys battled their tails off. I mean, we were down 17-0, and it didn't look good. And we were able to get back in the game." He's right about the fight. I wanted the finish too.

Next up: at Texas Tech, Thursday, Nov. 26, at 8:00 PM ET at Galaxy Stadium in Lubbock. Thanksgiving night, a short week, and a chance to end the regular season with a win. Wear the purple. Go Frogs!

articles.title: Utah vs TCU: Dampier Hits Simmons from 85 Yards, No. 2 Utes Clinch the Big 12 Title Game, 38-17
articles.byline: Aspen Mortensen, The Utah Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Utah Utes (11-0) 38, TCU Horned Frogs (5-6) 17, Sat., Nov. 21, Amon G. Carter Stadium, Fort Worth. Next: vs West Virginia, Fri., Nov. 27, 9:00 PM ET, Rice-Eccles Stadium, Salt Lake City
articles.text:
Fort Worth can keep the noise. I'll take this one: the Utah Utes beat the TCU Horned Frogs 38-17 on Saturday night at Amon G. Carter Stadium, and we are 11-0, 8-0 in the Big 12, and going to the conference title game. That's 17 wins in a row.

For a half, it looked simple. Dillon Curtis made a 45-yard field goal, Devon Dampier ran one in from 4 yards, and with 1:28 left in the second quarter Dampier found Braden Pegan for 68 yards. Utah 17, TCU 0. I started thinking about Friday already. That was dumb.

Jeremy Payne brought the Horned Frogs all the way back. He broke a 43-yard touchdown run in the third, added an 8-yard score, and Kyle Lemmermann tied it at 17-17 with a 32-yard field goal at 9:26 of the fourth. Payne ran 12 times for 108 yards. For a few minutes, that stadium was theirs again.

Then we went and took it back. Hunter Andrews scored from 2 yards at 5:46 to make it 24-17. Dampier let one fly to Larry Simmons, and Simmons finished an 85-yard touchdown at 2:59. Jackson Bennee, who came down with both of Adam Schobel's interceptions and returned them 99 yards, set up Dampier's 10-yard run at 1:53. Twenty-one points in 3:53. That's the Utah I stayed up for.

Dampier completed 18 of 28 throws for 278 yards with two scoring throws, and he added 62 yards and two scores on 21 carries. Simmons caught three balls for 114 yards. Elijah Elliss had two sacks. We didn't give the ball away once. Schobel, a freshman in his first start because Jaden Craig was out with a knee injury, went 15 of 31 for 106 yards.

Curtis missed a 38-yarder in the second quarter, and we were flagged 10 times for 90 yards. I'll live with the mess. The win is sitting there in the standings.

Next up: West Virginia at Rice-Eccles Stadium, Friday, Nov. 27, at 9:00 PM ET. Get the red out in Salt Lake. This thing is still rolling. Go Utes!
